free_tier.stated: EUR 3.99/month for EPYC-01 in Eygelshoven, Netherlands: 1 vCore on an AMD EPYC with host CPU passthrough, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB NVMe, a routed IPv6 /64 plus one IPv4, unmetered traffic at 300 Mbit/s, no setup fee. EPYC-02 is EUR 7.99/month for 2 vCores, 8 GB and 100 GB at 600 Mbit/s; EPYC-03 is EUR 15.20 for 4 vCores, 16 GB and 150 GB at 1 Gbit/s; the range runs to EPYC-08 at EUR 53.90 for 12 vCores, 64 GB, 300 GB and a 10 Gbit/s port. Prices include VAT where it applies and are billed monthly in EUR.

egress.terms: unmetered: no traffic limit; the uplink is provided according to the fair use principle and bandwidth may be temporarily throttled in the event of disproportionately high sustained usage

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.tooling: unusually well documented for this category: a public REST API of 48 endpoints with scoped keys, a Discord bot for power actions, backups and firewall rules, an AGPL-3.0 control panel published at github.com/virtbase/virtbase, a public status page and a looking glass
record.chaining: EUR 3.99 for 4 GB with no identity document and no phone number is the cheapest route among documented hosts to a machine that can actually be registered for, and the 48-endpoint API plus a Discord control plane makes it the one record here that a script can drive end to end without a browser; 300 Mbit/s caps what it can serve, so it is a control node or a small worker and not a mirror

limits.value: traffic is unmetered: no monthly volume allowance and no overage billing; the listed port speed is a hard rate limit at the hypervisor NIC, and the FAQ adds that bandwidth may be temporarily throttled in the event of disproportionately high sustained usage. So 300 Mbit/s on the entry plan is the wall, and a byte counter is not.

record.interface_detail: SSH on the guest; a public REST API of 48 endpoints, a web portal and a Discord bot manage power, backups and firewall rules.
record.tooling: ssh, the REST API and the per-server stateless firewall; any VPN or tunnel daemon the guest supports.
record.chaining: A dedicated IPv4 plus a routed IPv6 /64 for EUR 3.99 a month, with an Accept-by-default stateless firewall and upstream filtering of TCP and UDP: a UDP-capable endpoint with inbound ports and a routed prefix.

limits.value: 300 Mbit/s port speed, no volume cap

record.binding_note: There is no volume quota; 300 Mbit/s is the limit, and the FAQ allows a temporary throttle on sustained high use.

identity_cost.detail: A third-party post quoting the vendor says: No KYC, no ID document, no phone number, no verification call; the vendor privacy notice lists name, address, email address and phone number as examples of data collected when a contract is concluded. record.reliability_note: Billing is limited to EU-27 customers; the vendor FAQ allows a temporary throttle on sustained high use, which the offer post states as no post-quota throttle.
record.confidence_note: The price, resources, IPv4 and /64 lines are vendor page lines read on 2026-11-03 and agree with the third-party post. The identity statement rests on that post quoting the vendor, so the rung for identity is reported.
